title: Judd-Ofelt analysis and coherent spectroscopy of europium-based molecular complexes for quantum information applications
authors: Nicholas Lester Jobbitt, Sascha Weis, Timo Schweizer, Vishnu Unni Chorakkunnath, Evgenij Vasilenko, Tobias Haas, Barbora Brachnakova, Senthil Kumar Kuppusamy, Hartmut Schubert, Mario Ruben, Michael Seitz, David Hunger
abstract: Rare-earth-ion based molecular crystals are emerging as a promising platform for quantum information applications, combining long optical coherence times with the chemical tunability of coordination chemistry. Here we present a comprehensive optical characterisation of twelve Eu$^{3+}$-based molecular complexes, with a focus on the coherent $^{5}\text{D}_{0} \longrightarrow \ ^{7}\text{F}_{0}$ transition at $\sim$580 nm. Judd-Ofelt analyses are performed across all complexes, providing insights into ligand-field environments, local point-group symmetries, and the resulting branching ratios of the coherent transition. We find that lower point-group symmetry (C$_1$, C$_2$) yields higher branching ratios of the $^{5}\text{D}_{0} \longrightarrow \ ^{7}\text{F}_{0}$ transition, exceeding 1\% in several complexes. Optical inhomogeneous linewidths measured at 4.2 K reveal narrow linewidths for some complexes of below ten GHz, indicative of a highly ordered crystalline environment. Optical coherence measurements of one of the complexes, 5-Eu, yields an optical coherence time of $T_{\text{2}}^{\text{opt}} = 2.3~μ\mathrm{s}$ at 4.2 K, comparable to the best-performing molecular systems reported to date. Systematic characterisation and quantitative comparison will be key to find structure-property relations guiding rational design of optimised complexes for quantum information applications.
summary: This research characterizes $	ext{Eu}^{3+}$-based molecular complexes to optimize them for quantum information applications. By combining Judd-Ofelt analysis with advanced optical coherence measurements, the authors establish that lower local symmetry enhances the key transition's strength. The findings provide crucial guidelines for designing highly coherent solid-state quantum emitters.
main_problem: To develop rare-earth-ion based molecular complexes as a promising platform for quantum information applications by understanding and enhancing their optical coherence.
main_result: Lower point-group symmetry ($	ext{C}_1, 	ext{C}_2$) significantly increases the branching ratio of the coherent $^5D_0 ightarrow ^7F_0$ transition, and some complexes exhibit optical coherence times ($T_{	ext{2}}^{	ext{opt}}$) up to $2.3 \mu	ext{s}$ at $4.2 	ext{ K}$.
method: The study combines comprehensive optical characterization, Judd-Ofelt analyses to probe local symmetry, and advanced coherence measurements like two-pulse photon echo and spectral-hole burning.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{Eu}^{3+}$-based molecular complexes, utilizing the highly coherent $^5D_0 ightarrow ^7F_0$ transition ($\sim 580 	ext{ nm}$) as the quantum emitter. The analysis relies on crystal field theory and Judd-Ofelt parameters to link structure to optical properties.
key_observables: Optical coherence time ($T_{	ext{2}}^{	ext{opt}}$), branching ratios, inhomogeneous linewidths, and the ratio of electric-dipole to magnetic-dipole transition strengths.
important_parameters: Low point-group symmetry ($	ext{C}_1, 	ext{C}_2$), cryogenic temperature ($4.2 	ext{ K}$), and the crystal field environment.
main_assumptions: Judd-Ofelt theory is used, though the authors note its limitation in fully accounting for state mixing crucial for the nominally forbidden transition.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the $	ext{Eu}^{3+}$ energy levels and the measured coherence times/branching ratios for various complexes, comparing different measurement techniques (e.g., photon echo vs. spectral hole burning).
paper_structure: The paper systematically characterizes twelve complexes, performing Judd-Ofelt analyses to deduce local symmetry, measuring linewidths to assess crystalline order, and finally performing coherence measurements to quantify quantum memory potential.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the development of solid-state quantum emitters, providing structure-property relationships that guide the rational design of materials for quantum memory and quantum networking applications.

figures.caption: Fig. 1 Schematic showing the energy-level system of Eu3+. The coherent 5D0 −→ 7F0 transition is located at a wavelength of approximately 580 nm. Each state is comprised of three doubly-degenerate hyperfine states due to the I = 5/2 nuclear spin of both naturally occurring isotopes of europium.

Fig. 2 Molecular structures of: (A) 1-Eu, (B) 2-Eu, (D) 3-Eu and (E) 4-Eu, and the measured room temperature fluorescence spectra of (C) 1-Eu and 2-Eu, and (F) 3-Eu and 4-Eu. Excitation was provided at 532 nm. Insets with ×10 zoom are provided showing the coherent 5D0 −→ 7F0 transition located at ∼580 nm in addition to the 5D0 −→7F5, 6 transitions located between 720 and 850 nm.

Fig. 5 (A) - (C) Inhomogeneous linescans at room temperature of (A) 1-Eu and 2-Eu, (B) 4-Eu, and (C) 5-Eu and 6-Eu. (D) - (F) Inhomogeneous linescans at 4.2 K of (D) 4-Eu, (E) 5-Eu and (F) 6-Eu are also presented. Lorentzian fits were performed on all measurements to extract the optical inhomogeneous linewidths. Double Lorentzian fits were performed on the room temperature measurements of 1-Eu and 2-Eu and the 4.2 K measurements of 6-Eu, whereas all remaining measurements were fitted with a single Lorentzian. The resulting fitted values are presented in Table 2.
